findings: The source preserves only a three-table association/subquery implementation prompt and does not preserve schema, fields or one business result; the candidate explicitly declares its students/courses/scores example as a reference exercise.

The reference query has a coherent result grain of one student per row, uses both three-table join relationships, computes student aggregates in the outer query and a scalar global-score aggregate in the subquery.
The answer correctly distinguishes pre-aggregation WHERE semantics from aggregate HAVING semantics and warns against using DISTINCT score to hide data-model duplication.

Independent randomized differential testing over 12,000 fixtures matches an oracle for strict above-global-average selection, aggregate values and distinct course counts, including duplicate fact rows and empty scores.

The candidate explicitly scopes INNER JOIN no-score behavior, duplicate-fact semantics, NULL/empty behavior and execution-plan/index validation as contract or operational concerns rather than preserved source facts.
